Literature-informed assessment: The statement is near-term cautious (softening activity, elevated inflation) but medium-term constructive given decisive tightening and an explicit commitment to the 2% objective. The 75 bp hike to a 2.25–2.50% range and balance-sheet runoff are consistent with rules-based stabilization and the Taylor principle (Taylor; Clarida–Galí–Gertler) and with expectations-focused policy (Woodford). Emphasis on inflation expectations reflects the expectations-augmented Phillips-curve view that actual and expected inflation reinforce each other, and reducing inflation carries measurable welfare gains (Feldstein). Recognizing war-related supply shocks, the Fed’s readiness to accept some short-run output risk (Sims on monetary shocks’ real effects; Orphanides on real-time uncertainty) to preserve credibility is in line with lessons from the Volcker disinflation.

Most important sentence: “The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.”
